PMID:41393646.topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
PMID:41393646.setting: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust, large NHS hospital trust
PMID:41393646.standard: BOAST Standard 1: documented radial pulse, capillary refill time and individual radial, median (AIN) and ulnar nerve function in every child with a supracondylar fracture

cycle1.result: Individual nerve function documented in 4 (9.1%); 40 (90.9%) recorded only as 'neurovascularly intact'. Radial pulse documented in 19 (43%), omitted in 25 (57%). CRT documented in 30 (68%), omitted in 14 (32%). Post-cast X-ray in 29 (66%); 12 (27.3%) discharged in a cast without imaging.

PMID:41393646.other_findings: Single cycle; authors recommend an electronic neurovascular proforma and teaching, with a re-audit planned after an electronic checklist is introduced.

PMID:41641182.setting: Luton and Dunstable Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital, A&E department
PMID:41641182.standard: Group and save sample rejection rate of 10% or less (SHOT national haemovigilance guidance and local transfusion policy)

cycle1.result: 64/171 (37.4%) G&S samples rejected; 40 of the rejected samples taken in A&E. Causes: documentation errors 43 (67.1%), sample quality 13 (20.3%), labelling/ordering errors 8 (12.5%). 13 patients needed 2 or more repeat samples.

PMID:41641182.intervention: Training and competency sessions for A&E staff, standardised bedside labelling protocol, and a bedside G&S checklist attached to all blood collection trolleys (implemented April 2025).

cycle2.result: 14/84 (16.6%) samples rejected; 11 of 14 from A&E. Causes: documentation errors 8 (57.1%), sample quality 4 (28.6%), labelling/ordering errors 2 (14.3%).

PMID:41641182.other_findings: Direct cost per rejected sample £12 to £80 (average £30). The 10% target was still not met at re-audit and most rejections remained in A&E.

PMID:36457816.topic: Radiographs at cast removal in distal radius fractures
PMID:36457816.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, district general hospital (Dorset County Hospital), virtual fracture clinic referrals
PMID:36457816.standard: BOAST distal radius fracture guidance: no radiograph at removal of immobilisation unless there is clinical concern

cycle1.result: 20/46 (43.5%) had a radiograph at cast removal; none had a documented indication (0:20) and none altered management.

PMID:36457816.intervention: Education: results presented and BOAST guidance highlighted at the departmental morbidity and mortality meeting.

cycle2.result: 12/41 (29.3%) had a radiograph at cast removal (p=0.170); indication documented for 7 of 12 (p<0.001) and 2 altered management.

PMID:36457816.other_findings: Cycle 1 was retrospective and cycle 2 prospective. Number of clinic reviews, time in cast and complications did not differ significantly between cycles.

PMID:41211270.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic Department, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham
PMID:41211270.standard: BOA-endorsed orthoconsent.com complication lists: Consent Form 1 complete if all common, less common and rare complications documented

cycle1.result: Fewer than 50% of forms recorded several complications. Fixation (n=35): pain 6 (17%), catheterisation 2 (6%), altered leg length 4 (11%), avascular necrosis 0, hip stiffness 8 (23%), death 7 (20%). Hemiarthroplasty (n=39): altered wound healing 7 (18%), bone damage 22 (56%), death 8 (21%). THR (n=10): prosthesis wear 4 (40%), bone damage 4 (40%), death 2 (20%).

PMID:41211270.intervention: Results presented at departmental audit meeting; teaching sessions on consent practice and posters listing complications to document (June and July 2024).

cycle2.result: Fixation (n=51): pain 17 (33%), avascular necrosis 8 (16%) (p=0.019), death 10 (20%). Hemiarthroplasty (n=25): altered wound healing 10 (40%) (p=0.051), bone damage 21 (84%) (p=0.022). THR (n=18): prosthesis wear 11 (61%), bone damage 10 (56%), death 4 (22%); no THR change significant.

PMID:41211270.other_findings: Some items fell after the intervention, e.g. fixation blood vessel damage 89% to 80% and THR nerve damage 100% to 72%. Patients who signed Consent Form 4 were excluded.

PMID:42344576.setting: Department of Orthopaedics, tertiary care hospital
PMID:42344576.standard: RCSE and BOA operative note documentation standards (18 parameters in four domains)

cycle1.result: Domain compliance: patient identification 72%, intraoperative findings 65%, postoperative plan 58%, surgeon details 70%; overall adherence 68%.

PMID:42344576.intervention: Staff training programme and a new mandatory standardised operative note template, with laminated guideline cards and documentation mentors (July to October 2023).

cycle2.result: Patient identification 95%, intraoperative findings 95%, postoperative plan 90%, surgeon details 97% (all p<0.001); overall adherence 95% (p<0.001).

PMID:42344576.other_findings: Postoperative plan remained the weakest domain with 10% non-compliance at re-audit. Incident reports related to operative documentation fell by 25%.

PMID:35971362.setting: Orthopaedic trauma unit, William Harvey Hospital, district general hospital, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
PMID:35971362.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice (2014) operation note guidance, modified to 17 parameters; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: 10/17 parameters above 70% compliance; indication for surgery 45%, tourniquet time 20%, antibiotic prophylaxis 71%, closure technique 62%, detailed postoperative instructions 40%, estimated blood loss 7%.

PMID:35971362.intervention: Results presented at clinical governance meeting; surgeons educated on the typed electronic operation note template through live demonstrations, discussions and recorded videos.

cycle2.result: 14/17 parameters above 70%; indication 75%, tourniquet time 45%, antibiotic prophylaxis 89%, closure technique 86%, postoperative instructions 92%, estimated blood loss 8%. 25% of typed notes fully compliant versus none of the handwritten notes.

PMID:35971362.other_findings: DVT prophylaxis plan documentation regressed and blood loss and tourniquet time stayed below 50%. Mean parameters documented did not differ between typed (14.375) and handwritten (14.080) notes (p=0.449).

PMID:38655761.topic: Surgical site infection prevention in hand trauma
PMID:38655761.setting: International multicentre audit of plastic and orthopaedic units operating on hand trauma, via the Reconstructive Surgery Trials Network
PMID:38655761.standard: WHO global guidelines for the prevention of surgical site infection (e.g. antibiotic prophylaxis within 120 minutes before incision, chlorhexidine-alcohol skin preparation, no shaving, no prolonged prophylaxis)

cycle1.dates: End of November 2023 to end of July 2024 (planned)
cycle1.result: not reported (protocol only; minimum 20 consecutive patients per team)

PMID:38655761.other_findings: Published protocol with no results; secondary outcome is a description of current antimicrobial practice in hand trauma surgery.

PMID:36523668.topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
PMID:36523668.setting: Trauma unit, district general hospital, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
PMID:36523668.standard: BOAST guidance for supracondylar fractures in children: individual documentation of sensory and motor function of median, AIN, ulnar and radial nerves, radial pulse and capillary refill

cycle1.result: Full neurovascular documentation at A&E review 19 (39.6%), 'NVI' only 21 (43.7%), none 8 (16.7%). After backslab: full 16 (33.3%), none 24 (50%). Postoperatively (n=42): full 16 (38%), 'NVI' 5 (12%), none 21 (50%).

PMID:36523668.intervention: Supracondylar fracture assessment proforma (paper and electronic) and multidisciplinary teaching for emergency department and trauma staff.

cycle2.result: Full neurovascular documentation at A&E review 5 (19.2%), 'NVI' 18 (69.2%), none 3 (11.6%). After backslab: full 9 (34.6%), none 13 (50%). Postoperatively: full 10 (38.5%), 'NVI' 9 (34.6%), none 7 (26.9%).

PMID:36523668.other_findings: Full neurovascular documentation did not improve and fell at first review; gains were mainly in less incomplete 'NVI' entries. Mean time to surgery 1.3 then 0.96 days.

PMID:33133805.topic: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff compliance
PMID:33133805.standard: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff 2016 criteria and NHS Enhanced Recovery Partnership Programme criteria (including day one postoperative osteoporosis bloods)

cycle1.dates: November 2015 to May 2016 (whole audit; initial cycle two months)
cycle1.result: Full BPT met in 38.7% (12/31); no patient had FRAX or NHFS recorded; day one osteoporosis bloods requested in 61.3% (19/31); all other ERP parameters 100%.

PMID:33133805.intervention: Written reminders and M&M presentation on NHFS and FRAX, hip fracture scores added to the hospital smartphone app, and a reminder sticker on the operation note to request day one osteoporosis bloods.

cycle2.result: Full BPT met in 63.3% (19/30); NHFS recorded in 66.7% (20/30); day one osteoporosis bloods 90% (27/30).

PMID:33133805.other_findings: Lost BPT income of £8,265 in cycle 1; projected uplift £18,270 per year for intervention costs of £2.00.

PMID:32523827.setting: Orthopaedic department, District Headquarter Hospital, Rawalpindi, tertiary care training hospital
PMID:32523827.standard: RCS Good Surgical Practice (2014) operative note guidance

cycle1.result: Operative diagnosis 80%, peri-operative findings 72%, anaesthetist name 78%, assistant 88%, operating surgeon 90%, operation type 6%, time 62%, complications 10%, closure technique 12%, DVT prophylaxis 0%, time out 0%, postoperative orders 80%, signature 90%.

PMID:32523827.intervention: New dedicated orthopaedic operation note format based on RCS guidance, introduced July 2019 with staff briefing, posters, short videos and notices.

cycle2.result: Operative diagnosis 100%, findings 96%, anaesthetist 92%, assistant 93%, surgeon 99%, operation type, date and time 100%, complications 94%, closure 93%, DVT prophylaxis 90%, time out 100%, postoperative orders 100%, signature 95% (0.001<P<0.005).

PMID:32523827.other_findings: Text reports a total of 500 notes compared although 215 and 235 are given per cycle. Tissue removed or altered was still only 70% after the change.
